macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $64K as markets wait for fresh catalyst
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $63,800-$64,000 after a U.S. inflation report came in line with expectations, leaving crypto markets without strong momentum. Several reports also noted that Bitcoin briefly dipped below $64,000 before stabilizing.

items.title: Crypto market sees mixed price action, with altcoins showing selective strength
items.summary: Market coverage showed Bitcoin and Ethereum largely flat to slightly lower over 24 hours, while BNB, Solana, Tron, Hyperliquid, and Cardano posted gains of up to 4%. XRP and Dogecoin were reported lower on the day.

items.title: More than $175 million in crypto positions liquidated in 24 hours
items.summary: A market update reported that over $175 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the past 24 hours, with short sellers accounting for about $93 million of those losses. The same report said the global crypto market cap fell to about $2.17 trillion.

items.title: SEC to weigh tailored crypto offering rules as CLARITY Act awaits Senate vote
items.summary: A crypto market roundup said SEC commissioners are scheduled to meet on Aug. 14 to consider tailored rules for crypto offerings. The same report said the CLARITY Act is awaiting a Sept. 15 Senate vote.

items.title: South Korea tightens crypto transfer rules and extends Travel Rule coverage
items.summary: South Korea reportedly scrapped the 1 million won threshold for its crypto Travel Rule, extending it to all domestic VASP transfers. The move also tightens controls on transfers involving overseas exchanges and personal wallets.

items.title: Hawaii joins other U.S. states in banning crypto ATMs and kiosks
items.summary: A latest-news roundup reported that Hawaii will become the fourth U.S. state to fully ban cryptocurrency ATMs and kiosks, citing scam prevention. Minnesota, Tennessee, and Indiana were named as the other states with similar bans.

items.title: Morph launches non-custodial stablecoin payments platform
items.summary: A top crypto news roundup listed Morph's launch of a non-custodial stablecoin payments platform among the day's notable project developments. The listing suggests continued infrastructure activity in stablecoin payments.

items.title: MoneyGram brings Solana cash ramps to 170+ markets
items.summary: MoneyGram launched Ramps on Solana, giving developers cash deposit access in more than 25 countries and withdrawals across more than 170 countries and territories. The move expands the real-world payments use case for Solana-based applications.

items.title: Binance expands tokenized stock offering with bStocks growth
items.summary: Binance's bStocks reportedly surpassed $610 million and overtook xStocks within two months. Another report said Binance also supports third-party tokenized stock conversions to bStocks.

items.title: Trezor says customer shipping details were exposed in data breach
items.summary: Coinpedia and crypto.news both reported that a breach involving ShipMonk exposed shipping information for 13,689 Trezor customers. The reports did not indicate that seed phrases or wallet contents were compromised.

items.title: Charles Schwab adds Bitcoin and Ether trading to its platform
items.summary: A crypto news roundup reported that Charles Schwab has added Bitcoin and Ether trading to its $13 trillion platform. If confirmed, the move would mark another major traditional finance channel for crypto access.

items.title: Goldman Sachs plans ETF acquisition tied to bitcoin yield strategy
items.summary: A CNBC-linked video item said Goldman Sachs wants to turn bitcoin into a yield machine and is acquiring ETF provider Neos in a $2.3 billion deal. The report suggests continued institutional product development around bitcoin exposure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Gemini app reaches 1 billion users
items.summary: Google's Gemini AI assistant has reached 1 billion users, according to recent reporting, marking a major adoption milestone for the company’s consumer AI push. The app is now being discussed as keeping pace with OpenAI's ChatGPT in scale.

items.title: Microsoft simplifies Copilot by merging consumer and business apps
items.summary: Microsoft is consolidating its Copilot offerings into a single experience and removing several features, including AI-generated podcasts, Group Chats, Deep Research, and its Mico character. The change suggests a broader product cleanup as the company refines its AI assistant strategy.

items.title: General Catalyst leads $1.1B round into River AI
items.summary: Startup River AI, founded by xAI co-founder Igor Babuschkin, reportedly raised $1.1 billion in a seed-like financing round. The company is positioning itself around personal agents and advanced AI workflows.

items.title: Grok Bot launches as an autonomous AI coworker
items.summary: SpaceXAI and Cursor launched Grok Bot in early beta, pitching it as a 24/7 AI teammate that can perform multi-step digital work by operating software interfaces directly. The release adds to the growing trend toward agentic AI products that act across apps rather than only generating text.

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6-Cyber
items.summary: Reporting in the Indian technology press says OpenAI released GPT-5.6-Cyber, a purpose-built security model tied to its Daybreak Red approval gate. The model is described as part of a security-focused product line with token pricing aimed at enterprise and developer use.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly building 1-trillion-parameter Nemotron 4
items.summary: A report says Nvidia is developing Nemotron 4, a 1-trillion-parameter model intended to compete with leading open AI systems. If accurate, it underscores the continued escalation in frontier-model size and competition among major AI labs.

items.title: Meta strategy shifts back toward open-weight AI models
items.summary: Coverage of Mark Zuckerberg’s AI manifesto says Meta has resumed releasing open-weight models after a major strategy reset. The move reflects a broader industry split between closed, subscription-based models and open releases that can be downloaded and adapted.

items.title: Spotify plans labels for AI-generated artists
items.summary: BBC reporting says Spotify will add labels for AI-generated artists and remove them from recommendations. The policy change is part of a wider industry response to synthetic content and provenance concerns in music.

items.title: Amazon using Twitch to train generative AI
items.summary: BBC reports that Amazon is using Twitch content to train generative AI systems. The development highlights how major platforms are increasingly leveraging user-generated media as training data.

items.title: White House broadens AI safety framework to open models
items.summary: A recent digest cites reporting that the U.S. administration plans to extend voluntary AI safety frameworks to open-weight models as they approach frontier capability. That would bring more open-source-style systems into policy discussions that have mostly centered on closed models.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Game Informer says GTA VI is getting an 'extended look' on Netflix
items.summary: Game Informer reports that Grand Theft Auto VI will receive an extended look on Netflix on August 27, signaling a major new promotional push for one of gaming’s most anticipated releases. If confirmed by Rockstar or Netflix, this would be a notable cross-media marketing development.

items.title: The Verge reports Nvidia’s GeForce Now Linux app has left beta
items.summary: The Verge says Nvidia’s GeForce Now app for Linux is now officially out of beta, which is a meaningful cloud-gaming platform update for PC and Linux users. The move expands access to Nvidia’s streaming service beyond its earlier testing phase.

items.title: Nintendo says Oblivion Remastered is arriving on Switch 2
items.summary: Nintendo’s site lists The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered for Nintendo Switch 2, adding another major third-party title to the platform’s lineup. The same page also confirms Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is launching on Switch 2 on Aug. 28.

items.title: Gadgets 360 reports Ghost of Yotei is getting DLC and a roguelike mode
items.summary: Gadgets 360 says Ghost of Yotei will receive its first story expansion and a new single-player roguelike mode in October. If accurate, that would make it one of the larger post-launch content announcements in today’s gaming news cycle.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero gameplay deep dive reportedly set for Sony’s next State of Play
items.summary: Gadgets 360 reports that Phantom Blade Zero will get a gameplay deep dive at Sony’s next State of Play show. That would mark another major showcase appearance for the action title ahead of launch.

items.title: Sony announces a limited-edition Marvel’s Wolverine PS5 bundle and accessories
items.summary: Gadgets 360 says Sony has unveiled a limited-edition Marvel’s Wolverine PS5 bundle along with matching accessories. The reported release adds more platform branding around one of PlayStation’s headline exclusives.

items.title: CD Projekt Red confirms layoffs tied to Project Sirius
items.summary: Gadgets 360 reports that CD Projekt Red has confirmed layoffs affecting Project Sirius, the Witcher multiplayer spinoff. The development underscores ongoing turbulence around the studio’s broader multiplayer plans.

items.title: Remedy says Alan Wake 2 has surpassed 3 million copies sold
items.summary: Gadgets 360 reports that Alan Wake 2 has crossed 3 million copies sold nearly three years after launch, according to Remedy. That sales milestone is a notable commercial update for one of the studio’s most prominent recent releases.

items.title: GamingBolt says Mafia: Definitive Edition is out Aug. 14 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5
items.summary: GamingBolt reports that Mafia: Definitive Edition is scheduled to release on Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 on Aug. 14, alongside an Omertà Collection reveal. That makes it a near-term release announcement worth tracking.

items.title: Gamerant highlights Helldivers 2's new 'Force of Law' Warbond
items.summary: Game Rant says Helldivers 2 has revealed the Force of Law Warbond, giving players a new content drop to look forward to in the cooperative shooter. The announcement continues the game’s steady post-launch live-service cadence.
